properties.areaDesc: Matagorda Islands; Brazoria Islands; Galveston Island; Bolivar Peninsula
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 10 at 6:54AM CDT until October 10 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard and away from rocks, jetties, and piers. If
caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH THIS EVENING

properties.description:

across parts of central North Dakota this morning. Motorists
should be prepared for rapidly changing conditions and use extra
caution traveling. Use low beam headlights and be extra cautious
at intersections and railroad crossings.

The fog is expected to dissipate by 10 AM CDT.

properties.areaDesc: Bryan, GA; Chatham, GA
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 7:48AM EDT until October 10 at 9:15AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Bryan County in southeastern Georgia...
Chatham County in southeastern Georgia...

* WHEN...Until 915 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 747 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Minor flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
- The earlier area of heavy rainfall has since lifted north of
Chatham County. Additional showers will pass through over the
next 60 to 90 minutes and could produce brief periods of light to
moderate rain.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tybee Island, Midtown Savannah, Coffee Bluff, Windsor Forest,
Hunter Army Airfield, Wilmington Island, Downtown Savannah,
Hutchinson Island, Fort Pulaski National Monument and Montgomery.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Report flooding directly to the Charleston National Weather Service
at 1-888-383-2024 or email your reports to nws.charlestonsc@noaa.gov.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 915 AM EDT THIS MORNING

properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued October 10 at 4:30AM PDT until October 11 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures as low as 33 to 36 degrees will result in frost
formation.

* WHERE...Upper Hood River Valley County, especially near Parkdale.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 9 AM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Chances for sub-freezing temperatures below 32
degrees are high in Parkdale and Dee (70-90%) tonight into Sunday
morning. However, the majority of the Upper Hood River Valley
should remain above freezing with lows of 33 to 36 degrees,
including in Odell.
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender outdoor plants from the cold.
Consider temporarily moving outdoor potted plants indoors if they are
sensitive to cold temperatures.

Consider temporarily covering sensitive plants with a lightweight
cotton fabric (i.e., bedsheets, thin blankets), as this will help
retain heat and provide frost protection for your plants.

properties.areaDesc: Charleston, SC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 7:23AM EDT until October 10 at 9:30AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
At 723 AM EDT, City of Charleston Emergency Management reported heavy
rain in Downtown Charleston. Flash flooding is already occurring with
several road closures across the city.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...City of Charleston Emergency Management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
North Charleston, Mount Pleasant, James Island, Johns Island, West
Ashley, Downtown Charleston, Fort Sumter, Daniel Island, Folly
Beach and Kiawah Island.

An area of intense rainfall moved through the Folly Beach, James
Island, Johns Island, West Ashley, and Downtown Charleston areas and
produced 1 to 2 inches of rain. The heaviest rain has now lifted
northward but light to occasionally moderate rain will continue.
Additional rounds of heavy rain could develop through mid morning.
City of Charleston Emergency Management reported several roads closed
across the Downtown Charleston area and flash flooding is ongoing.
Additionally, a inundation depth sensor on Ogier Street near Calhoun
Street reported an inundation depth of over half of a foot.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Report flooding directly to the Charleston National Weather Service
at 1-888-383-2024 or email your reports to nws.charlestonsc@noaa.gov.
